description:
Phase 4. The distributor's mutating operations, each one transaction prefixed by the Lock fence: (a) recruit for a demanded/uncovered tag - phase-a pipeline (Foreman new_worker with shard_id+idle params, lock at epoch, unlock at worker-reported durable version via typed pull_sources like bootstrap), then commit materializers/<tag> = {worker_id, node}; commit abort replaces the old delta-rejection as both the supersession signal (stop :normal) and the orphan-cleanup trigger. (b) heal on materializer death (monitor-driven, event-based like teamTracker; slow verify sweep as insurance): recruit replacement, commit the entry. With this, bootstrap stops creating data-tag workers (gaps left ABSENT; placeholder covers) - completing stall-only-for-tag-0. Proxies fold the committed mutations; displaced-but-alive workers still self-detect at the next push until phase 6 delivers in-band.

RUNNER OBLIGATIONS from the PR #186 audit (also documented on Lock.check/3): (1) read the owner key first and the write key ONLY when the owner is not my_owner - the steady-state branch ignores current_write (pass nil); an unconditional write-key read puts a read conflict on a key the same transaction writes, serializing all concurrent same-owner distributor transactions (FDB deliberately reads it only in the previous-owner branch). (2) Pass absent-key reads through as nil UNDECODED - nil is protocol-meaningful (fresh cluster / stomped lock) while Values.decode_lock_uid(nil) is a decode error by design. (3) Optional, unported by decision: FDB's DDEnabledState operational kill switch has no analogue; if wanted later, a single killswitch key suffices.
ADDITIONAL OBLIGATION from the PR #189 audit (2026-08-21): add an integration test driving two CONCURRENT fenced transactions through a REAL resolver (not scripted commit seams) to pin the abort-on-write-after-read-version behavior the fence's safety rests on — unit tests verify the wire contract; only static analysis has verified the resolver side. Also inherited: check-fenced commits must add a read conflict on the write key ONLY when the previous-owner branch read it (see Lock.check/3 doc).
FIT CONSIDERATION from the PR #190 audit: for repo traffic the placeholder park is ~50ms per attempt (the builder's fetch timeout), with the repo backoff loop doing the actual waiting. When recruitment lands, consider a hold-aware fetch timeout for known-placeholder routes (or accept the retry-loop smoothing as-is — it is bounded and self-healing); decide with measurements, not speculatively.
title: Recruit and heal transactions under the lock
